resources.string: Not armed yet. Nothing will slap you… for now.
Usage access is off. Tap to fix.
Put the phone down or get slapped.
Slap Me needs Usage Access, a special Android permission, to know how long you\'ve been using your phone without a break.
Which app is in the foreground, and when it came to the front. Nothing inside your apps.
To count continuous use during your focus time, to skip calls, navigation and the camera, and to apply your list of distracting or allowed apps.
Nowhere. It stays on this phone. Slap Me has no internet access and never collects or shares your data.
During your focus time, Slap Me counts how long you\'ve been on your phone without a break.
Go over your limit and you get a warning, then a cartoon slap that sends you back to the home screen.
Every slap shortens the next limit; a real break resets it. Fun, a bit annoying, never harmful.
In the list that opens, pick Slap Me and turn on \"Permit usage access\". Then come back here.
The slap appears over whatever app you\'re in, and this is also what lets Slap Me send you to the home screen. Turn on \"Allow display over other apps\" for Slap Me.
You\'ll get a warning before each slap with a button to snooze, and a short note after it.
Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery. Set Slap Me\'s battery use to \"Unrestricted\" (or \"No restrictions\") so it keeps watching.
On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones, also turn on Autostart for Slap Me so it comes back after a restart.
Slap Me can\'t tell which app is open: calls, maps and the camera would count, and your app lists don\'t work.
Display over other apps is off
Without it the slap can\'t appear and can\'t send you to the home screen.
You won\'t get the warning or the Snooze button before a slap.
Your phone may stop Slap Me in the background to save battery. Set its battery use to \"Unrestricted\".
Your phone stopped Slap Me in the background recently. Set its battery use to \"Unrestricted\".
On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones, also turn on Autostart.
